title: Scaling Laws of Graph Neural Networks for Atomistic Materials Modeling
problem: GNNs for atomistic materials modeling remain small (millions of parameters) compared to LLMs (billions); lack of scaling guidance limits accuracy and applicability to complex materials discovery tasks.
motivation: Accurate atomistic modeling drives drug discovery and materials science; understanding GNN scaling laws can unlock performance gains comparable to LLM scaling benefits.
method: Develops foundational GNN with billions of parameters trained on terabyte-scale datasets; incorporates LLM-inspired training techniques (efficient data/model management) to enable large-scale GNN training and deployment; explores three scaling dimensions: architecture, dataset size, and training method applicability.
key_novelty: First large-scale GNN study (billions of parameters, TB-scale data) for atomistic materials modeling, applying LLM-inspired scaling techniques to GNN architectures.
contributions: Scaling laws for GNNs: model size, dataset volume, and accuracy relationships
Foundational billion-parameter GNN model optimized for atomistic materials
Advanced LLM-based training techniques adapted for GNN architectures
Codebase and insights enabling future large-scale GNN development
baselines: Smaller GNN models for materials modeling
limitations: Generalization beyond atomistic materials not discussed; specific accuracy improvements not quantified in abstract.
primary_theme: Scaling laws for billion-parameter GNNs in atomistic materials modeling
